prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1291; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed head-on collision in which the insured vehicle was struck by another vehicle. The claimant reports neck pain and has retained counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report obtained. The reporting officer confirms the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene and that the vehicles came to rest in the positions described.

Entry 3: Photographs of the damage received from the insured. The front-end damage on the vehicle is consistent with the reported impact and the reported speed.

Entry 4: Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy and that coverage was active on the loss date. Nothing in the file points to damage existing before the policy period began.

Entry 5: Vehicle history checked. No prior damage claims or repair records are on file for this vehicle.

Entry 6: Attorney letter received with medical authorization. Claimant's initial treatment began within a day of the collision and followed a typical course of evaluation, imaging, and physical therapy.

Entry 7: Prior records requested. The claimant had a minor strain in the same area of the neck several years ago, which resolved fully with treatment. The reported injury pattern fits the force of this collision.

Entry 8: Recorded statement from the claimant obtained through counsel. The claimant added a few small details about the moments after impact, but the core account matches the original report.

Entry 9: No independent witnesses have come forward. The photographs confirm several details of the scene but do not show the collision itself.

Entry 10: Treatment notes reviewed. Therapy visits tapered off as the claimant's symptoms improved, and the treating provider's notes describe steady recovery.

Entry 11: File reviewed for handling. Liability and injury evaluation are proceeding on the current documentation, with a settlement discussion to follow once the final treatment summary is received.
